title: tool-saga-execution-shim: deterministic retry protection and streaming handshake for multi-tool calls
author: Priya Narayanan
release_notes: Introduces a lightweight Tool Saga shim to provide deterministic idempotency keys for multi-tool/parallel invocations, safer streaming handshakes when tools are invoked during a stream, and explicit retry/dedup metadata exposed in the API. Backwards-compatible surface; small SDK opt-ins required for deterministic retries.
description:
Context: customer workloads and internal evaluations exposed two brittle failure modes when models requested multiple tools in-parallel during streaming responses: (1) races between the streaming token path and tool-return callbacks that caused partial/duplicated stream frames, and (2) non-deterministic retries leading to duplicated tool effects when the same tool was called across retries. Motivation: make multi-tool calls ergonomic and safe across streaming and non-streaming flows while retaining OpenAI function-call compatibility for users migrating to Redwood. This PR implements a 'Tool Saga' execution shim and OpenAI-compat behavior flags.

Design summary: the Tool Saga is a short-lived orchestration layer attached to a single model response call. It assigns per-tool idempotency keys (deterministic from request id + tool slot + nonce) and tracks lifecycle (pending/returned/failed). Streaming handshake: when a model emits a tool-call frame during a streaming session, the runtime will suspend downstream token emission for that stream until all non-optional tool responses are either returned or a configured grace timer elapses. This prevents interleaving partial tokens with tool-injected content. Retry protection: retries are coordinated using dedup keys persisted in a lightweight in-memory store (with optional tiled persistence behind the shard) for the duration of the request + 30s window. OpenAI compatibility: the shim exposes an opt-in compatibility mode that maps tool-calling frames to OpenAI-style function_call objects and guarantees that the final structured output matches the function_call/arguments schema.

What changed (high level): commits implement the saga orchestrator in runtime/tool_saga.py, a streaming handshake in runtime/stream_controller.py, the OpenAI compatibility adapter in api/openai_compat_adapter.ts, SDK helpers in sdk/python/redwood/tools.py and sdk/typescript/src/tools.ts, and e2e harnesses under test/e2e/tool_saga. Added docs in docs/guide/tools.md and a console note in console/changes/tool-visibility.md. Tests: unit tests for determinism and idempotency, integration e2e for streaming + parallel tool calls with simulated latency and flaky tool endpoints.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc referenced (ENG-1209)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] SDK update with backward-compatible opt-in flag
- [x] Docs + Console note
- [x] Perf run (microbenchmarks included)

API/behavior notes for users: By default behavior is backward compatible: tools invoked via the classical sync path are unchanged. To enable deterministic retries and streaming handshake, users must set "tool_saga": true on the request envelope. SDKs expose a helper call run_with_tools(..., tool_saga=True) which opts a request into the new flow. When enabled the response will include a top-level "tool_saga" object in the response metadata containing per-tool ids and statuses. The object is intentionally small and transient; it is not persisted to the long-term audit log unless the workspace opts in via console settings (see docs).

Migration notes: existing consumers that inspect raw streaming tokens should audit for the new handshake semantics: streams will pause briefly during tool resolution; the overall ordering of model output and tool-injected content is guaranteed. For function-call compatibility, the OpenAI adapter returns a final structured payload under the same key path as OpenAI (function_call.name and function_call.arguments) when opt-in is used. SDKs automatically translate into native call wrappers when available.

Implementation details and rationale: Idempotency keys are derived from HMAC(request_id || tool_slot) using a signing key available in the request context; this keeps keys deterministic without exposing request ids to downstream tooling. The dedup store is an in-process bounded LRU with optional persistence layer bound to the serving shard; it is sized to impose minimal memory overhead for typical burst sizes. The streaming handshake uses a short (configurable) grace period to avoid long stalls for best-effort optional tools; the default is 250ms with exponential backoff for subsequent tool waves in the same response stream. Tests show median added tail latency of ~12ms for ordinary streams and up to 140ms for heavy parallel tool rounds (acceptable given correctness benefits). We also added opt-out hooks for latency-sensitive customers.

Review conversation (summary): Marco Li: asked for explicitness about HMAC key rotation and suggested adding tests that simulate key rotation during retries. Denise Park: requested stronger assertions in the e2e harness for ordering guarantees and asked to add metrics to track handshake stalls. Ethan Brooks: flagged a potential race in stream_controller when tool callbacks race with commit tokens; author fixed with a small atomic state transition and re-pushed. Follow-ups: added metric runtime.tool_saga.handshake_pause_ms and enhanced test coverage for flaky tool endpoints.

CI & validation: initial CI run failed a flaky e2e test (test_tool_saga_stream_pause under high-latency simulate); root cause was nondeterministic timing in test harness which was hardened. Final CI: all checks passed (linux/tests, windows/tests, js/ts-lint, py-lint, integration/e2e, microbenchmarks). Perf run shows 0.9% median throughput regression in worst-case due to handshake overhead; acceptable per ENG-1217 signoff.

Files changed (high level): runtime/tool_saga.py, runtime/stream_controller.py, runtime/handlers/tool_invoke_handler.py, api/openai_compat_adapter.ts, sdk/python/redwood/tools.py, sdk/typescript/src/tools.ts, test/e2e/tool_saga/test_stream_pause.py, docs/guide/tools.md, console/changes/tool-visibility.md

Related work: builds on prior tool-execution PRs and orchestration improvements (see ENG-990 and the function-calling compatibility work). Linear links included above.

Merge: squash and merged after green CI and two approvals. Rolling watch for first 48 hours post-deploy; no regressions observed in canary.
